text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Crown Prince, meeting the people of Karak, says Jordan is "a country of initiative and capable of utilising its resources."
- Kabariti tells exporters the government has successfully continued to attain monetary stability and was able to reduce foreign debt while managing to eliminate distortions in the economy.
- Jordan's finance and energy ministers arrive in Baghdad and to begin official talks with Iraqi counterparts on Monday.
- The cold front recedes and rains result in over 100 injuries and traffic accidents across the kingdom.
- Kabariti visits southern Tafila governate and says a new national project will be set up to create thousands of jobs.

- Kabariti tells leading exporters and businessmen in a dinner hosted by Jordan Exporters Association that the government's policy is based on "offering incentives to manufacturers, encouraging exporters and attracting investors."
- Justice Minister al-Dughmi says an amended law that allows bail for defendants charged in bounced cheques cases when it previously forbade it would help ease problems.
- Labour Minister says government policy is geared to ease poverty and unemployment.
- Government plans to liberalise prices of car spare parts soon, officials say.
- Crown prince say our fight is not against unemployment but against culture of shame that shuns menial work.
- Kabariti assures Tafilah residents that solutions to their problems under way.
